summary: Koshin Suzuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a researcher between 1995 and 1998.

Koshiro Tamaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo (DLitt 1959). He held posts at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo (1964–1976), Tohoku University, and Nihon University (1979–1986).

Kosho Kawamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Shunkyo Katsumata, Koshiro Tamaki, and Yoshiro Tamura. He worked at Toyo University and later taught at Minobusan and Hamamatsu Universities.

Kosho Uchiyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a master's in Western philosophy from Waseda University and studied under Kodo Sawaki. He taught at Miyazaki Catholic Seminary (1937–1939) and served as abbot of Antai-ji (1965–1975).
Koshu Itahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sendai Daiichi High School, the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy, and Tohoku University (~1949–1953) under Teruji Ishizu.

Kosuke Nakazawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at Rissho University and as a member of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra, both attested in 2001.

Kotatsu Fujita was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, he studied under scholars including Hajime Nakamura. He served at Osaka University, as professor at Hokkaido University (~1969–1991), and led Sapporo Otani Junior College.
Koun Kajiyoshi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1928 to 1931 and held an academic post at Taisho University from ~1949 to 1975.
Koyo Sakaino was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai and held posts at Toyo University and Komazawa University.
Koyo Shimizu is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoko Takeuchi and served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1995.

Koyu Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his master's and DLitt from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Encyclopaedia of Buddhism Department, Nishogakusha University, and served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (1972–2000).

Krishna Kamal Bhattacharya was an Indology scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and University and Presidency University. He later held teaching posts at Presidency University (1862–1872) and Surendranath College (1891–1903).

Krishna Kanta Handiqui was an Indologist who studied at Calcutta, Oxford, Paris, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Jagannath Barooah College (1930–1948) and Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (1948–1957), and founded the Hemalata Handique Memorial Institute.

Krishna Mohan Banerjee was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and linguistics who studied at Hare School, Presidency University, and Bishop's College under Alexander Duff. He taught at Hare School and became Second Professor at Bishop's College in 1852.

Krishnanath Chatterjee is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under teachers including Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amarasvar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Kristin Johnston Largen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Colby College and Harvard University under Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. She has held posts at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College.

Kristina Myrvold is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She was a doctoral candidate and editor at Lund University (attested 2005, 2008) and became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Linnaeus University, attested in 2014.

Kristofer Schipper was a sinologist who studied in Paris. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, École Pratique des Hautes Études, CNRS, Collège de France, and Leiden University, and later taught at Fuzhou University and Minnan Normal University.

Krisztina Teleki is a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA in Tibetan and Mongolian at Eötvös Loránd University (~1997–2009), where she also served as a research fellow around 2010.
